seo.title: Docs · zapzero
seo.description: How to install and use zapzero: macOS permissions, shortcuts, your voice, tags, calendar with Claude and settings.

sections.title: How to use zapzero.
sections.intro: Install it, give macOS the right permission, clear your WhatsApp from the keyboard and let your Claude handle the calendar.

chapters.title: Install
chapters.body:
The app (recommended)

  1. Download zapzero for Mac (Apple Silicon), open the .dmg and drag zapzero to Applications.
  2. Open the app. The first time, macOS says it couldn't verify it (it isn't signed by Apple yet): go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
  3. Give zapzero Full Disk Access (see macOS permission) and open it again.

The app runs zapzero's server on your Mac and opens the panel in a window. Quit the app and the server stops. It needs WhatsApp Desktop and Claude Code, below.

From the terminal

You need three things, all on your Mac:

  • WhatsApp Desktop, the official app, linked to your phone. Linking syncs about 3 months of messages; older chats show in the list without text.
  • Claude Code, logged in with your Claude subscription. It triages your chats and writes the drafts. Install.
  • Bun 1.3 or newer, to install and run it. bun.com.

Optional: an OpenRouter key. It unlocks Jev, a faster and cheaper classifier for triaging thousands of chats (US$ 0.09 for 1,600). Without it, Claude triages everything.

In Terminal:

git clone https://github.com/vibegui/zapzero && cd zapzero
bun install
cp .env.example .env    # optional: paste your OpenRouter key
bun run setup

setup checks everything, takes the first copy of your chats, builds the panel, creates the server that starts when you log in, and prints the panel link with your password.

Setup questions

Setup asks two things, once: the panel language (Portuguese or English) and which AI reads your chats: your Claude (subscription), a local model on Ollama (nothing leaves your Mac) or OpenRouter. To change later, run setup again or bun run setup --lang=en --llm=ollama.

Before reading your WhatsApp it runs an automatic test on a fake database. If that fails, it stops without having read anything.

chapters.title: macOS permission
chapters.body:
With the app

In System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access, click + and pick zapzero in Applications. The server runs inside the app and inherits the permission. After updating the app, check that it is still on.

From the terminal

macOS protects WhatsApp's folder. Without permission it shows a dialog every time zapzero reads your chats. You fix it once, in two steps.

1. During setup: your terminal

If setup says it can't read WhatsApp's database, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access, add the terminal app you use and run bun run setup again.

2. After: zapzero's server

The server that runs in the background is its own program, built by setup:

~/Library/Application Support/zap/bin/zapzero

Give that file Full Disk Access. These two commands open the right pane and show the file in Finder; drag it into the list:

open "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles"
open -R ~/Library/Application\ Support/zap/bin/zapzero

Don't give it to bun. Every script that runs with Bun would get access to your whole disk. That's why the server is a separate program: only it gets the permission.

It's once: setup creates that program a single time and zapzero updates don't touch it, so the permission keeps working.

chapters.title: Open the panel
chapters.body:
Open http://127.0.0.1:8810/?t=<password>. Setup prints the full link; the password is also in ~/Library/Application Support/zap/token.

Every 15 minutes zapzero takes a fresh copy of your chats, triages what changed and drafts replies for everyone waiting on you.

On your phone or another computer

Put the panel on your private Tailscale network (never Funnel, which is public):

tailscale serve --bg --set-path=/zap http://127.0.0.1:8810

chapters.title: Clear your WhatsApp
chapters.body:
The sidebar sorts chats into categories: Important & urgent, This week, Older than a week, Waiting on them, Groups and Cleanup. Below them are your tags (Clients, Hiring, Family…), each with its own color.

Start with Important & urgent. Every chat comes with a draft in your own voice.

  • Y opens the chat in WhatsApp with the text typed in. You hit Enter.
  • Dates, amounts, yes or no come as choices: press 1–9 or click one. When you answer the last one, the AI rewrites the whole sentence in your voice.
  • Don't like the draft? E edits, R asks for another.
  • O opens the chat in WhatsApp with nothing typed, for context.

Shortcuts

KeyWhat it does
Y or EnterReply in WhatsApp
EEdit the draft (⌘ Enter replies while editing)
1–9Pick a choice in the draft
RNew draft
CTurn the calendar event on or off
DDone, no reply
AArchive
SSkip for now
IIgnore this person forever
OGo to the chat in WhatsApp
J / KNext / previous
/Search by name
ZUndo

Everything you did lands in Feitas (done), each with an undo button.

chapters.title: Your voice
chapters.body:
After the first read, the AI writes who you are (where you live, work, family, who matters) and how you write (length, slang, emoji). Open Seu jeito in the sidebar and accept or fix each part: triage and drafts follow it.

It also learns from you. Every draft you fix before sending becomes an example for the next ones. Once a week your fixes turn into suggested rules in Seu jeito; tick the ones that make sense and they join your guide.

chapters.title: Tags
chapters.body: Every chat gets a tag: who the person is or what it's about. Click a tag to see only those chats. Once a day the AI suggests new tags when it sees a recurring subject; accept one with Criar tag and it re-sorts the rest.

chapters.title: Group digest
chapters.body: Once a week your Claude reads the ~30 busiest groups and writes, for each, what happened (topics, decisions, dates) and what involves you: who mentioned you, asked or requested something. Open Resumo dos grupos in the sidebar; the ones that need you come first. Gerar agora makes a fresh one (about 2 minutes).

chapters.title: Calendar with your Claude
chapters.body:
When you reply agreeing to a day and time, the panel offers to create the event in your calendar. When you press Y, zapzero calls your Claude Code, which creates the event with a call link using the calendar connector it already has.

  • If the other person sent their e-mail in the chat, it shows up ticked for the invite.
  • If not, ask for it in the draft (+ pedir o e-mail). When they answer, the chat comes back to Important & urgent to finish the invite.

Needs: Claude Code with a calendar connector (Google Calendar on claude.ai, for example). It may only create and update events, and only when you reply. zapzero never sees your calendar.

Pending

In the sidebar, Proposta de agenda gathers meetings with a day and time that came up in your chats over the last few days, yours or theirs ("dinner Thursday 8pm?"). Click Marcar and your Claude creates the event (or finds the one that exists) and invites the ticked e-mails; Não dismisses it.

zapzero already knows the e-mail of anyone in your Mac's Contacts, or anyone who sent it in the chat, so most of the time it doesn't need to ask.

chapters.title: Use it from Claude
chapters.body:
zapzero runs a local MCP at http://127.0.0.1:8810/mcp, on your Mac only, behind the panel's password. In the panel's footer, Connect to Claude copies the command; paste it in Terminal:

claude mcp add --scope user --transport http zapzero \
  http://127.0.0.1:8810/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <password>"

Its tools: inbox, chat, stats, decide (done, skip, archive, ignore, only in zapzero's list), undo and refresh. None of them sends a message.

Skill and terminal

Setup installs a Claude Code skill. In any Claude conversation you can ask "who's waiting on me on WhatsApp?", "what should I answer Marina?" or "how long do I take to reply?".

In Terminal, the same API:

bun run zap api inbox          # categories and chats
bun run zap api stats          # reply performance
bun run zap refresh            # read and triage now

Claude only proposes. Nothing is sent, archived or marked as read without you.

chapters.title: Settings
chapters.body:
All optional, in the repo's .env. After a change, restart: launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/dev.zapzero.server.

VariableWhat it does
OPENROUTER_API_KEYUnlocks Jev for triage (faster and cheaper)
ZAP_LLMclaude (default), ollama or openrouter
ZAP_CLAUDE_MODELClaude Code model; default haiku
ZAP_TRIAGEllm triages with Claude even with an OpenRouter key
ZAP_REFRESH_MINHow often it reads again, in minutes (default 15; 0 turns it off)
ZAP_PORTPanel port (default 8810)
ZAP_DATAWhere copies and state live (default ~/Library/Application Support/zap)
ZAP_CALENDAR_TOOLThe calendar tool Claude may use
ZAP_OLLAMA_MODELLocal Ollama model (default: the first one installed)

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
chapters.body:
macOS keeps asking for permission

zapzero is missing Full Disk Access (see macOS permission). If you deleted the data folder, run setup and grant it again.

"snapshot: no answer in 120s" in the log

macOS is waiting on a permission dialog. Look for an open window and check the permission above. The panel keeps the last copy meanwhile.

No drafts show up

Claude Code must be installed and logged in. Run claude once in Terminal to check. The log is ~/Library/Logs/zapzero.log.

Reply opened WhatsApp on the wrong chat

Some chats with people outside your contacts have no number saved. Then the text goes to your clipboard: paste it with ⌘ V in the chat.

Uninstall

launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/dev.zapzero.server
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.zapzero.server.plist ~/.claude/skills/zapzero
rm -r ~/Library/Application\ Support/zap    # copies, drafts and decisions

chapters.title: Privacy
chapters.body:
• Read-only: zapzero never writes to WhatsApp's files.
  • Nothing sent without you: it types, you hit Enter.
  • No server of ours: your chats stay on your Mac. Only the excerpt needed goes to your Claude (and to Jev, if you turn on OpenRouter).
  • Message text is treated as data, never as instructions to the AI.
  • Open source (MIT): github.com/vibegui/zapzero.

sections.fine: zapzero isn't affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. Names and messages on this page are fictional.
